purpose: Measure the change in the graduated OXO cup over each successful short- or medium-pulse train using the cup camera.
physical_measurement: A withdraws concentrate from the cup. B returns it. The observed liquid volume corresponds to a complete train. Mean volume per pulse divides the directed transfer by the acknowledged pulse count.
before_exposure: Each before image is the preceding completed dose image in controller order. Native cup images were saved after the controller stopped. The before-to-command interval uses the PNG file completion time. The failed first 50 ms B attempt reported a busy device and issued no command. The succeeding B retry uses the preceding 50 ms A image.
flow_time: Full-cycle flow uses the acknowledged duration including the final pause used in repeating service.
image_geometry: Coordinates refer to native 4656 by 3496 sensor images rotated 180 degrees. The listed x and y crop origins locate each retained lossless crop within that upright image. Each crop was compared pixel for pixel with the source and contains the liquid arc and every neighboring graduation used by its local cubic interpolation.
meniscus: The near contact is the lower transition from the bright surface rim into dark liquid at the front of the cup. On the saved contact sheet, green dashes show the robust cubic through clear glass and cyan circles show the six reading positions. Red ink and the two immersed hoses obscure portions of the arc.
primary_fit: An inspected height window localizes the liquid band. A green/red downward intensity gradient through each clear optical section gives candidate boundary pixels. A robust cubic is fitted across the unprinted front arc with residual rejection. The source frame supplies its own printed stems, graduations and surface fit.
graduations: The three q sightlines cross the quarter-cup ruler and the three t sightlines cross the thirds-cup ruler. Their horizontal offsets follow the tilt of each printed stem. Detected red tick centers on each sightline are paired with the printed cup values. Monotone piecewise cubic interpolation gives the nominal volume at the liquid contact. The bracketing tick indices are zero based.
pair_algorithm: Subtract the before volume from the after volume on each matching sightline. The nominal signed change is the median of these six differences. The sightline columns show their extrema. The linear-interpolation column instead interpolates between the two surrounding printed marks on each sightline.
model_sensitivity: Secondary fits read the location at one quarter, one half and three quarters of the local rim-to-dark intensity contrast in unobstructed glass. Each uses a robust cubic across the cup. An additional fit uses a quadratic at half contrast. The same-model range takes the least and greatest whole-train change across those choices and the primary fit. The independent-endpoint range also permits different fits at the two endpoints.
accuracy: Sightline and model ranges describe sensitivity to reading these particular images. The columns share the same camera, vessel and graduations. Absolute volumetric accuracy depends on the cup graduation tolerance, viewing geometry and liquid contact. A traceable reference volume and an absolute accuracy bound were unavailable. All optical calculations use the printed cup geometry.

archive_only_verification.method: Independently recenter the local red print from the retained native crop, read the surface at each sightline from the saved cubic, and recompute the PCHIP on the local support ticks.
